name: Solenne Auric Datalink Bracelet
description:
Wide-cuff bracelet in 22-carat gold-analog plating over a titanium substrate, inlaid with a continuous band of lab-grown black opal that shifts between deep violet and copper-green depending on ambient light. Embedded along the inner face is a passive data-chip array — twelve chips, each holding encrypted social credentials, financial access keys, or personal records. The clasp is a Japanese-style fold-over in white gold-analog, stamped with Solenne's Spire atelier mark.

Worn as jewelry. Functions as an entire secure wallet, identity suite, and social passport.
functionality: Twelve passive NFC chips store financial credentials, encrypted identity data, and social access keys. BCI-synced release — only the wearer's neural signature unlocks the chip array for write access. Read-only pings are blocked by the titanium substrate except at designated contact points. No power source required.
what_it_says: Everything you need to know about this person is in that bracelet, and you will never be authorized to read it.
story_hooks: A bracelet matching this description appeared in a Tier-1 pawn shop — the chip array was wiped, but the clasp stamp is genuine Solenne, and the atelier has no record of the sale.
The black opal shifts color in proximity to certain encrypted signals — a feature Solenne officially denies building in.
One chip on every Solenne Datalink bracelet is factory-reserved and cannot be written by the owner; what Solenne stores there is the subject of considerable Spire paranoia.
